title: Typed checks with a fixed passing answer
statement: Write each judged check as a typed question with its passing answer fixed in advance, and let code, not the judge, turn the answer into a verdict.
example: A yes-or-no check expecting yes holds when the judge's value is 0.5 or more and its answer clears the support gates, fails below that, and is unclear when the gates fail.
detail: Every block in the lesson engine lists its judged checks as an id, a label, a typed question (yes or no, a choice or a score) and the answer that passes it, and a block's checks go to the judge in one batched decision that carries only the questions and their state, never the passing answers (`g9/transformer/src/judge.js`). One verdict function, used at play time as well, reads each answer: one that fails the judge's support gates is unclear, never a pass, and otherwise the check holds only when the answer goes the expected way. Code then decides from the verdicts alone: a required check that does not hold keeps the block from shipping (`g9/transformer/src/transform.js`).
against: How sure counts as sure has not been calibrated: a required check held at p 0.6 in the first live proof, and the precision of the judge's checks is not yet measured (`g9/transformer/v01/proof-2026-10-09.json`, `g9/transformer/v01/QA.md`).

evidence.quote: A check holds only on positive … evidence: an answer that fails the support gates is "unclear", never a pass.
